conviction_note: Two sourced but already-circulated facts offset: the stock is down 21% in a month into a Q1 the company pre-guided as weak (bar low, last print beat $0.87 vs $0.63), against a European potato-crop shock that threatens the FY27 cost guide; no unpriced company-level number found, so p_up sits at 52 on a ~11-point absolute move.
bar: Consensus EPS ~$0.58 (year-ago $0.74) and revenue ~$1.654B, from marketbeat/futunn previews (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-lamb-weston-lw-expected-to-announce-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-09-29/); company Q1 guide of flat sales and EBITDA down low teens (Q4 call, July 24 2026) is consistent with it. Two agreeing estimate sources, consistent with company guide.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest 6.29M shares at 2026-08-31 (+420,860), ~4.7% of free float per Ortex, borrow cost 0.48% and abundant (https://ortex.news/articles/177222/lamb-weston-heads-into-earnings-with-options-traders-at-peak-caution); not a crowded short. Put/call ratio 2.08 (more than 2 sd above its 20d average), put volume +829% on 9/18; sealed baseline carries no usable chain (skew null, total OI 66), so the skew is not measurable and the put-call read is the only directional statement. Stock -20.7% over 20d, -7.4% over 5d, 37% below 52w high.

findings.finding: Stock is washed out into a Q1 the company already told the market would be weak (flat sales, EBITDA down low teens, NA price/mix down low single digits, international down); consensus EPS $0.58 sits on that guide, and the last print beat by $0.24 on volume growth (sixth straight quarter of volume growth), so a print merely in line with the pre-guided shape faces a depressed bar.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the 21% one-month fall, target cuts to $41-$50 and put-heavy options already embed the weak Q1; this is a lean toward a bounce on a low bar, not a hidden number.
findings.independence: Price action and Ortex put/call data (https://ortex.news/articles/177222/lamb-weston-heads-into-earnings-with-options-traders-at-peak-caution) show the same washed-out positioning; Q4 beat figures from https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-jpmorgan-chase-co-has-lowered-expectations-for-lamb-weston-nyse-lw-stock-price-2026-09-30/

findings.finding: European potato crop deterioration (EU-4 output ~25% lower on reduced acreage and heat/drought yields, Dutch yields ~14% below) raises FY27 procurement-cost uncertainty in EMEA, the reason Stephens cut its target to $50 and a risk to the FY27 EPS guide of $2.95-$3.25 at the Q1 call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Dec 2025 guide cut produced -25.94% and the April print -8.94%; guidance changes have driven this name's biggest moves, but the July guide was met with only +0.81%.
findings.why_not_priced: Already in the price: Stephens (Sept 28), JPMorgan (Sept 30), BNP and Barclays cut targets on it and the stock fell about 14% in 8 sessions; proxy sized small, and Q1 uses old-crop inventory so the cost lands in later quarters.
findings.independence: Stephens target cut citing lower acreage, weaker yields and smaller sizing (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-stephens-cuts-lamb-weston-nyse-lw-price-target-to-5000-2026-09-28/); separate trade-press source above. Not the same document as the first finding.

searched_and_found_nothing: Usable option chain / implied move (baseline unusable_chain, ATM legs not two-sided)
Counterparty/peer print since Q4 call (McCain, Aviko, Simplot do not report in window; no direct read-through found)
September 2026 restaurant traffic series (only May 2026 -2.0% and older data surfaced; no fresh September number)
Company-level unpriced document (no new 8-K, 10-Q footnote or hiring signal found after July 24)

rejected_candidates.candidate: Put/call ratio 2.08 and put-volume spike as a bearish signal
rejected_candidates.detail: Folded into positioning_check and the first finding's p_up reasoning rather than filed as a separate finding; it is the same washed-out-positioning fact.

baseline_tension: What I found agrees with the heavy put positioning and the -21% run-up on the cost side but I lean slightly against them on a low bar, so I stay near 50 rather than trade against a skew I cannot measure.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 and 7: reaction history (last big beat only +0.81%) and the unmeasurable skew plus put-heavy positioning kept the bounce finding small (+1.5 to +1.6) and p_up at 52

Lesson 5: European potato crop item is a trade-press and analyst proxy for FY27 cost, already cited in target cuts, so its weight was cut from -2.0 to -1.2 and it is filed as guidance, not the quarter
Short interest checked (4.7% of float, not crowded) so no squeeze shrink applied beyond this
